docs.title: IT Procurement Intelligence Platform
docs.text:
Buying software and hardware for a company, automated end to end — from a vendor's quote landing in a folder to a signed contract and a matched invoice. AI reads the documents; people step in only where a decision is needed.

Explore Architecture Functional Workflow Admin Control Panel

docs.title: The flow in one line
docs.text: Document in (upload, email or the ./inbox/input folder) → read, classified and validated → purchase request → approval by spend tier → contract generated → e-signature → signed PDF stored → order → delivery → invoice matched. Every step is an event on Kafka, and the right person gets an email at each one.

docs.text: You want to… Read Understand the problem and the solution Introduction and objectives See how the parts fit System architecture, Functional workflow Know what one agent does Agents Run or administer the platform Control Panel, Deployment Call the API APIs Check the final review checklist Final checklist

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
./run.sh                        # whole stack; ends with "All services healthy."
./scripts/seed-demo-data.sh     # demo vendor, requests, licences, stock

Open http://localhost:8080 and sign in as admin@demo.example.com (password DemoPass123!). Then drop a quote PDF into ./inbox/input and watch it on Control Panel.

docs.title: Control Panel
docs.text:
The administrator's single place to run the platform: sidebar → Control Panel (/app/control-panel, admin only). Each section is a tab; a deep link opens one directly: /app/control-panel?section=<key>.

Section (key) What it shows Routine tasks Overview (overview) Files in each folder, approvals and signatures waiting, failed events; drop folder, Kafka, MinIO and e-signature status See at a glance what needs attention; click a figure to open its section Documents (documents) Input / Being read / Processed / Failed folder counts; each dropped file's stage; every failure reason Follow a document to its request and contract; see why a file failed Processing and logs (processing) Live Kafka event log (filter by topic, time, text, correlation id); failed events (dead-letter queue) with the error Trace one document across services; spot stuck consumers Approvals (approvals) Every request waiting for a decision, with its spend tier and SLA countdown Open a request at its Approval step to decide Notifications (notifications) Every email template; recent notifications with status Create, edit, preview, turn off or restore a template; add copy recipients Contracts and e-signatures (esign) Every contract with Unsigned contract PDF / Signed contract PDF links and Pending E-Signature / E-Signature Complete status Download either PDF; open a contract to sign or send it Email Settings (email) Company SMTP server (password stored encrypted) Set up and test sending from your own domain Storage (storage) MinIO bucket, object count, latest files Check storage without the MinIO console Administration (admin) Links to System Health, Users, Controls, Business Rules, Audit Manage users, rules and authority

docs.title: Document lifecycle (folders)
docs.text:
./inbox/input/       drop files here
./inbox/.processing/ being uploaded, then held while the pipeline reads the file
./inbox/processed/   read successfully
./inbox/failed/      rejected or failed; <file>.error.txt holds file, time, document id and reason

A file is moved only when the pipeline has finished, so a scan that turns out to be blank ends in failed/, not processed/.

docs.title: E-signature tracking
docs.text:
Document Status Unsigned contract PDF Pending E-Signature Signed contract PDF E-Signature Complete

Both PDFs are fetched through the app with the admin's own session, so no one needs MinIO or an e-signature provider's site. The signed copy appears as soon as the contract is signed.

docs.title: Notification templates
docs.text:
1. Pick a template on the left (it shows the event that sends it and who receives it).
  2. Edit the subject and body; click a placeholder to insert it ({{ request_id }}).
  3. Optionally add copy recipients, or untick Send this email.
  4. Preview shows it with sample values; Save applies it to the next email.
  5. Restore default brings the built-in text back; New creates a template that services send by name.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
Business problem. Approvals happen over email with no record of who may approve what; stock and licences are tracked in spreadsheets; invoices are matched to orders by eye.

Objectives. Route each purchase request to the right approvers by spend and budget, enforce approval authority and separation of duties, keep approvals moving with SLAs, and manage inventory, licences, sourcing and invoice matching.

Input Output A request from the app, or a quote from document.classified An approved or rejected request (approval.decided per level), reserved stock, reorder suggestions, matched invoices

docs.title: 2. Technical implementation
docs.text: Part Detail Components FastAPI API, Temporal ApprovalWorkflow (one per request), Kafka consumers, order monitor, reorder service, invoice ledger AI models IsolationForest + SHAP for licence-usage anomalies Tables purchase_requests, approval_history, approver_assignments, approval_delegations, budgets, inventory, licenses, license_usage, catalog_items, rfq_*, goods_receipts, invoice_matches API /api/requests, /api/inbox/{level}, /api/authority, /api/budgets, /api/inventory, /api/licenses, /api/catalog, /api/rfqs, /api/invoices, /api/tds, /api/orders, /api/ops, /email-action/* Communication Consumes document.classified, contract.signed, business_rule.updated; publishes approval.requested, approval.decided, budget.threshold_crossed, rfq.*, goods.received, reminder.due (through the outbox) Deployment API + Temporal worker from one image; Temporal and Redis required

docs.title: 3. Functional implementation
docs.text:
1. Spend tier from business rules: ≤ ₹500 auto-approved, ≤ ₹5,000 manager, above that manager + finance; over-budget requests get a finance step.
  2. Workflow: for each level, wait for a decision. Only someone assigned to that level, within their limit, and not the requester may decide (separation of duties). Decisions come from the app or a single-use email link.
  3. SLA: reminders at 50 % and 80 %; on breach, escalate to the next level, or reject at the last level.
  4. After approval: approval.decided for the final level triggers the contract; hardware stock is reserved, or backordered with a reorder suggestion.
  5. Invoices: line-level three-way match (order, receipt, invoice) with 1 % tolerances; a mismatch holds payment.

docs.title: 4. Results and evaluation
docs.text:
Measure Result Source Licence anomaly model ROC-AUC 0.954, AP 0.873 on test (vs 0.687 for utilisation alone) docs/results/licence-anomaly.md Tests 275 unit/integration tests; budget_flow.py, sourcing_flow.py, invoice_lifecycle.py (71/71) scripts/test-service.sh

Limitations. Synthetic licence data; a real company's login logs would need re-tuning of the thresholds (business rules license.anomaly_*).

docs.title: Assistant (chatbot)
docs.text: Owned by Anooj.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text: Answers questions in plain language ("What uptime does our SaaS contract commit to?", "How many requests wait for approval?") from the platform's own data, without showing anyone data they may not see.

docs.title: 2. Technical implementation
docs.text: Part Detail Model Ollama on the host: llama3.2:3b for answers, nomic-embed-text for embeddings Retrieval document_embeddings (pgvector): contract clauses, document text, business rules and current records, re-indexed every minute; access checked per chunk Intent first Greetings, remarks and topic-only messages get a direct reply; licence anomalies come from live scores API /api/chat/*

docs.title: 3. Functional implementation
docs.text: Decide intent → retrieve the chunks this user may see → answer only from them, citing the source (CT-…, DOC-…, PR-…, a rule key) → say so when nothing relevant is found.

docs.title: 4. Results and evaluation
docs.text: tests/e2e/chatbot_eval.py: 20/20 questions answered as expected, including access limits (a requester asking for bank details is refused). 66 unit tests. Without Ollama the rest of the platform works; the assistant can't answer.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
Business problem. Every action must be tied to a real, verified person with the right role, and the procurement rules (thresholds, SLAs) must change without a release.

Objectives. Accounts with email verification, secure sessions, roles (requester, approver, finance, admin), and a business-rules engine that admins edit live.

Input Output Sign-up, login, rule edits JWT access tokens (15 min) + refresh cookie (7 days); rules served to every agent; business_rule.updated

docs.title: 2. Technical implementation
docs.text: Part Detail Security argon2id passwords, breached-password check (HaveIBeenPwned), lockout after 5 failures, single-use hashed email links, CSRF on refresh Tables auth_users, auth_tokens, auth_revoked_refresh_tokens, business_rules, business_rule_history API /api/auth/* (register, verify, login, refresh, logout, forgot/reset, users), /api/admin/business-rules Migrations Alembic (alembic_version_auth_service); each new rule is seeded by a migration and has a behaviour test

docs.title: 3. Functional implementation
docs.text:
• Identity always comes from the JWT, never from a request body.
  • Every agent reads rules through shared/rules_engine (5-minute cache, refreshed on business_rule.updated).
  • A rule change records who changed it, when and why.

docs.title: 4. Results and evaluation
docs.text: • 110 tests; auth_flows.py e2e 42/42 (sign-up, verify, reset, lockout, enumeration, rate limits).

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
Business problem. Contracts are copied from old files, emailed for signature and lost on shared drives; deadlines to cancel renewals are missed; nobody checks the vendor before signing.

Objectives. Generate the contract from the approved request, send it for e-signature, track signing and keep the signed copy, remind before notice deadlines, and decide whether a vendor may be signed at all.

Input Output approval.decided (final level) A contract (text + PDF), sent for signature; contract.generated, contract.signed; signed PDF and signature certificate; vendor risk score and clearance

docs.title: 2. Technical implementation
docs.text: Part Detail Components Contract service (Jinja2 templates → text → PDF), built-in e-sign, clause router, renewal workflow (Temporal), risk scorecard and collectors, clearance (services/clearance.py) AI models Legal-BERT fine-tuned on CUAD (clauses and obligations), regex rules as fallback Tables contracts, contract_obligations, sla_credits, risk_scores, risk_rulesets, vendor_decisions, vendor_evidence, vendor_sanctions_screenings API /api/contracts (list, detail, generate, send-for-signature, sign, document, signed-document, signature-certificate, esign/documents), /api/vendors/{id}/risk, /clearance, /api/webhooks/esign Communication Consumes approval.decided, document.classified; publishes contract.generated, contract.signed, risk.score.updated, contract.obligation.due, notification.send (signer email), reminder.due Deployment API + Temporal worker; sanctions list in a volume (./scripts/download-sanctions.sh)

docs.title: 3. Functional implementation
docs.text:
1. Generate only after the final approval level (a manager's approval of a manager + finance request waits for finance).
  2. Send for signature automatically (rule contract.auto_send_scope): the signer, an authorised signatory, gets an email with a signing link.
  3. Clearance before signing: a sanctions match or prohibited country blocks signing outright; a high-risk or unrated vendor needs the signer's explicit acknowledgement.
  4. Sign: typed or drawn signature, consent, SHA-256 seal of the contract and signer; the request moves to ordered; the requester and vendor are emailed.
  5. Track: the Control Panel lists every contract as Pending E-Signature or E-Signature Complete with its unsigned and signed PDFs; a reminder goes to the signer after 3 days.
  6. After signing: clauses and obligations extracted; renewal reminders counted back from the notice deadline.

docs.title: 4. Results and evaluation
docs.text:
Measure Result Source Clause extraction on 102 CUAD contracts F1 0.85 / 0.80 / 0.91 (renewal, notice, expiry) vs rules 0.50 / 0.19 / 0.02 docs/results/clauses.md Risk ruleset vs old random forest ROC-AUC 0.738 vs 0.715; 22 red-team profiles all handled docs/index.html#risk Tests 321 unit/integration tests; risk_flow.py 49/49; obligation_flow.py scripts/test-service.sh

Limitations. The built-in seal is an unkeyed hash (tamper-evident only as far as the audit log is trusted); a legally recognised provider is a future step.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
Business problem. Quotes, invoices and purchase orders arrive as PDFs, scans and photos. Retyping them is slow and error-prone, and fraud (fake invoices, changed bank details, look-alike vendors) hides in the paperwork.

Objectives. Take documents in from any channel, read them, decide what they are, extract their fields with a confidence for each, validate them, match the vendor, and send to a person only what needs a person.

Input Output A PDF / PNG / JPEG by upload, email or the ./inbox/input folder A classified document with extracted fields, confidences and validation results; the event document.classified; the file moved to processed/ or failed/

docs.title: 2. Technical implementation
docs.text: Part Detail Components API (app/api/documents.py, vendors.py, control_panel.py), worker (app/worker.py): Kafka consumer, drop-folder watcher (inbox_watcher.py), email intake (email_intake.py), pipeline (services/pipeline.py) AI models pdfplumber (text PDFs), Docling (scans), PaddleOCR (images, deskew + upscale), TF-IDF + logistic regression classifier (keywords as fallback), LayoutLMv3 cross-check Storage MinIO for files; tables documents, pipeline_checkpoints, vendors, vendor_payment_change_requests, email_intake API /api/documents/* (upload, list, detail, file, validation, review), /api/vendors/*, /api/gst/*, /api/admin/control-panel/* Communication Publishes document.ingested, document.classified, vendor.matched, vendor.payment_details_flagged, reminder.due; calls approval-inventory POST /invoices/match Deployment Docker image shared by API and worker; ClamAV and MinIO required; models cached in a volume (./scripts/download-models.sh)

docs.title: 3. Functional implementation
docs.text:
1. Intake: type checked from the bytes, size ≤ 25 MB, ClamAV scan (fails closed), stored in MinIO, documents row and document.ingested in one transaction.
  2. Drop folder: the worker polls ./inbox/input every 3 s, claims a file once its size is stable, uploads it like a UI upload, holds it until the pipeline ends, then moves it to processed/ or failed/ (with .error.txt: file, time, document id, reason).
  3. Read: in a separate process with a 120 s limit; no text → failed with a readable reason.
  4. Classify (quote / invoice / PO / other) and extract fields with per-field confidence; LayoutLMv3 cross-checks.
  5. Validate: vendor match (look-alike names flagged, first-seen bank details held for a second person), currency → INR, GST and e-invoice QR, invoice ledger match, duplicates.
  6. Decide: overall confidence < 80 % or any flag → review queue; otherwise automatic. Each stage's result is stored (pipeline_checkpoints) and shown on the document page.
  7. Exceptions: a dependency down → back to pending, retried after 1–4 min, failed after 5 attempts; a sweep re-queues stranded documents every minute.

docs.title: 4. Results and evaluation
docs.text:
Measure Result Source Classifier (held-out document kinds) Macro-F1 1.00 vs keywords 0.84 docs/results/classifier.md Extraction, text PDFs 100 % of fields docs/results/extraction.md Extraction, images ~49 % of documents fully right (with preprocessing) same Tests 373 unit/integration tests; document_pipeline.py e2e (corrupt, empty, huge, wrong type, outages) scripts/test-service.sh

Limitations. Poor phone photos are read correctly only about half the time; those go to review. Improvement: the research study's calibrated gate would let more clean invoices skip review at a guaranteed error rate.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
Business problem. People miss approvals and signatures because nobody tells them; when they are told, the message text is buried in code.

Objectives. Email the right person at every stage (users, approvers, signers, vendors), urgently or in a daily digest, from templates an administrator edits in the Control Panel; keep a log and an in-app feed.

Input Output 17 Kafka topics (approvals, contracts, reminders, budgets, RFQs, deliveries…) Emails (Mailpit in development, SMTP in production), notification_log, the in-app feed and bell

docs.title: 2. Technical implementation
docs.text: Part Detail Components Kafka consumer (app/kafka/consumer.py), dispatcher (urgent vs digest), template store (services/template_store.py), directory (who receives), digest loop Templates Built-in Jinja2 files app/templates/*.j2; overrides and new templates in notification_templates, rendered in Jinja's sandbox API /api/notifications/log, /feed, /unread-count, /read-all; admin: /api/notifications/templates (list, get, create, edit, reset, preview) Deployment One container; reads other services' tables read-only to resolve recipients

docs.title: 3. Functional implementation
docs.text:
Stage Who is emailed Approval needed (each level) The people assigned to that approval level SLA reminder The approvers of the waiting level (signer, finance or reviewers for other reminders) SLA missed, escalated The next level's approvers, told it was escalated Approval outcome The requester Contract sent for signature The signer, with a signing link Contract generated / signed The requester; the vendor's contact when signed Budget, obligation, RFQ, delivery, risk, offboarding Budget owner, obligation owner, vendors, requester, procurement

Templates without code changes. An admin edits subject, body, extra recipients (copies) and on/off for any email, or creates a new template. A save is checked first: the text must parse, and a built-in may only use the placeholders its event carries. If an edited template still fails when sending, the built-in is used, so an email is never lost. A template turned off is logged as skipped.

docs.title: 4. Results and evaluation
docs.text:
• 125 tests: every template renders with its event's documented payload, recipients per event, editing and sandboxing, digest routing.
  • Live check: an edited template with an extra recipient was received by both addresses in Mailpit; restoring the default brought the built-in back.

Limitations. Role mailboxes without an assigned person fall back to placeholder addresses (dept_manager@users.procurement.local); production needs real distribution lists.

docs.title: Communication
docs.text: Channel Used for HTTP/REST through the gateway Browser → services (JWT bearer token) Kafka events Service → service hand-offs (document.classified, approval.decided, contract.signed…); written to an outbox in the same transaction as the change Direct HTTP inside Docker Four synchronous calls: invoice matching, the assistant reading data, minting email-approval links Temporal gRPC Starting and signalling workflows SQL Each service to the shared Postgres HMAC-signed webhook External e-signature callback (/api/webhooks/esign)

docs.title: Data flow (one document)
docs.text:
1. A document arrives and is scanned by ClamAV, stored in MinIO and recorded; document.ingested is published with the row.
  2. The worker reads, classifies and validates it and publishes document.classified.
  3. A quote becomes a purchase request (approval.requested); a Temporal workflow waits for each approval level (approval.decided).
  4. After the final approval a contract is generated and sent for signature (contract.generated); signing publishes contract.signed and the request moves to ordered.
  5. notification-agent emails the right person at every step.

docs.title: Future enhancements
docs.text: Area Enhancement E-signature Connect a legally recognised provider (DocuSign / Documenso clients exist but are off); a keyed seal instead of an unkeyed SHA-256 Deployment Kubernetes manifests, TLS between services, managed Kafka and Postgres Documents Better accuracy on poor scans (images read correctly ~50 % of the time; PDFs 100 %) ERP Push approved orders and matched invoices to an ERP (SAP, Tally) Notifications Teams / Slack channels besides email; real distribution lists for role mailboxes Selective automation Use the research study's calibrated gate in production so more invoices skip review at a guaranteed error rate Vendors A vendor portal: vendors submit quotes and see order status

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: The platform takes a document from arrival to a signed contract and a matched invoice with no manual hand-offs, while keeping people in charge of the decisions that matter: approvals, signatures and anything the system is unsure about. Failures are visible (the Failed folder, failed events, the validation result of every stage), every step is audited, and an administrator runs it from one Control Panel. It is a working, tested prototype (1,276 automated service tests, end-to-end suites through the gateway) that runs on one machine with Docker Compose.

docs.text: One PostgreSQL database, shared by all services. Each service creates and migrates its own tables; base tables come from shared/db/init.sql.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: Original documents live in MinIO (bucket documents, key <document id>/<file name>). Contract PDFs are rendered from the stored contract text when downloaded, so the database holds the source of truth.

docs.title: Functional workflow
docs.text: Figure 2. Functional flow. Yellow: inputs; purple: automated steps; blue: decisions; pink: a person acts; red: failure or stop; green: success. Source: docs/assets/functional-flow.mmd, rendered by scripts/render_diagrams.py.

docs.title: Steps and decisions
docs.text: # Step Decision / exception Outcome 1 Ingestion: upload, intake mailbox or ./inbox/input Allowed type, size, virus-free? No → rejected; a drop-folder file moves to failed/ with a .error.txt 2 Read: pdfplumber, Docling or PaddleOCR Any text? Finished within 120 s? No → document failed with the reason; drop-folder file → failed/ 3 Classify and extract: quote / invoice / PO / other, fields with confidence 4 Validate: vendor match, currency, GST, duplicates, invoice match Confidence ≥ 80 % and no flags? No → manual review queue 5 Route: quotes start a purchase request; invoices are matched to orders Spend tier (business rule) ≤ ₹500 auto-approved; ≤ ₹5,000 manager; above, manager + finance 6 Approve: each level's approvers are emailed Decided before the SLA? Reminders at 50 % / 80 %; escalation on breach; rejection ends the request 7 Contract: generated from the template with the approved data Vendor cleared? Sanctions match → signing blocked; high risk → signer must acknowledge 8 E-signature: signer emailed a signing link Signed? Reminder after 3 days 9 Store and track: signed PDF and certificate kept; request → ordered Requester and vendor emailed; Control Panel shows E-Signature Complete

docs.title: Status transitions
docs.text:
Item Statuses Document pending → processing → classified (or failed); retried after an outage, failed after 5 attempts Drop-folder file input/ → .processing/ → processed/ or failed/ Purchase request pending_approval → approved / rejected → ordered → partially_received / fulfilled → partially_invoiced / invoice_received Contract draft → pending_signature → signed (later terminated / expired)

Purchase-request transitions are enforced by a state machine (shared/lifecycle.py) and a database check constraint.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Buying IT for a company (laptops, software licences, SaaS subscriptions) passes through many hands. A vendor sends a quote, someone types it into a request, approvers are chased by email, a contract is drafted and signed, and the invoice is finally checked against the order by eye.

This platform automates that chain with five cooperating services ("agents"). They read the documents, route approvals, generate and sign contracts, score vendor risk and email the people involved. People approve, sign, confirm deliveries and review anything the system is unsure about.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Read procurement documents automatically: classify quotes, invoices and purchase orders, and extract their fields with a confidence for each.
  2. Route approvals with enforced authority: spend tiers, approver assignments, separation of duties, SLAs with reminders and escalation.
  3. Generate contracts and collect e-signatures from the approved data, and keep the signed copy.
  4. Check vendors before money moves: duplicate and look-alike vendors, bank-detail changes, sanctions, risk scorecard.
  5. Keep people informed: an email at every stage, from templates an admin can edit.
  6. Give administrators one place to run it: the Control Panel.
  7. Audit everything: every decision and status change is recorded.

docs.title: Existing system
docs.text:
In a typical company today:

  • quotes and invoices arrive by email and are retyped into a spreadsheet or ERP;
  • approvals happen over email or chat, with no record of who could approve what;
  • contracts are copied from an old Word file, emailed for signature and saved somewhere on a shared drive;
  • invoices are matched to orders by hand;
  • nobody checks whether a vendor's bank account changed or the vendor is on a sanctions list until something goes wrong.

docs.title: Challenges
docs.text: Challenge Why it is hard Documents vary PDFs, scans and photos, different layouts, OCR noise Trusting automation A wrong total or vendor must not slip through; the system has to know when it is unsure Approval rules change Thresholds and approvers differ per company and change over time Many steps, many services A failure in the middle must not lose a document or leave a request half-done Fraud Fake or duplicate invoices, changed bank details, look-alike vendors Visibility Administrators need to see where every document and contract is without opening five tools

docs.title: Proposed system
docs.text:
Five agents, each owning one part of procurement, cooperate through events:

Agent Responsibility Document & Vendor Takes documents in (upload, email, drop folder), scans for viruses, reads and classifies them, extracts and validates fields, matches vendors Approval & Inventory Purchase requests, approval workflows by spend tier, budgets, inventory, licences, RFQs, invoice matching Contract & Risk Generates contracts, built-in e-signature, renewals and obligations, vendor risk scorecard and clearance Notification Emails and the in-app feed, from templates editable in the Control Panel Auth Accounts, roles, and the business rules admins change live

A sixth service, the assistant (chatbot, owned by Anooj), answers questions about requests, contracts and vendors from the platform's own data.

Design principles:

  • One home page per item (request, contract, document, vendor, licence); lists and the Control Panel link to it.
  • Events, not direct calls: a change and its event commit together (transactional outbox); consumers retry and park failures in a dead-letter queue.
  • Humans where it matters: low confidence, high value or high risk goes to a person; everything else flows.
  • Rules, not code: thresholds, SLAs and tiers are business rules an admin edits.

docs.title: Technology stack
docs.text: Layer Technology Frontend React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS ("Ledger" design system) Gateway nginx (only public port, :8080) Services Python 3.11, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy (async), Pydantic Messaging Kafka API on Redpanda, SASL/SCRAM login and ACLs per service Workflows Temporal (approvals, renewals) Database PostgreSQL 16 with pgvector (one shared database) Files MinIO (S3 API) Cache / locks Redis 7 Virus scan ClamAV Email Mailpit in development, any SMTP server in production Document AI pdfplumber, Docling, PaddleOCR, LayoutLMv3 cross-check, TF-IDF + logistic regression classifier Contract AI Legal-BERT fine-tuned on CUAD (clauses, obligations), regex fallback Licence AI IsolationForest with SHAP explanations Vendor risk Deterministic 100-point scorecard, sanctions screening (OpenSanctions) Assistant Ollama (llama3.2, nomic-embed-text), retrieval over pgvector Observability Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Promtail, Temporal UI, MLflow Packaging Docker Compose (22 containers), run.sh

docs.title: APIs
docs.text: Everything goes through the gateway at http://localhost:8080/api/…. Each service also serves interactive OpenAPI docs on its own port in development (http://localhost:8001/docs … 8005/docs).

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Auth: Authorization: Bearer <access token> from POST /api/auth/login. The refresh token is an httpOnly cookie. Identity always comes from the token.
  • Responses: {"data": …, "meta": …}; errors are {"error": {"code": "…", "message": "…"}}.
  • Idempotency: create endpoints accept an Idempotency-Key header.
  • Correlation: every response carries X-Correlation-ID; search it in the Control Panel's Kafka log or Grafana.
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST localhost:8080/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@demo.example.com","password":"DemoPass123!"}' | jq -r .data.access_token)
curl -s localhost:8080/api/contracts/esign/documents -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

docs.title: Issues found in this review
docs.text:
• Stale image: notification-agent's image was built before the SMTP-settings commit added cryptography, so its tests failed to start and the running service was out of date. Rebuilt; after any change to a service's requirements.txt, rebuild that service.
  • Escalation emails went to the level that missed its SLA, as a placeholder address, with a generic subject. Fixed (see A2).
  • SMTP encryption key (needs a decision): compose doesn't pass SMTP_ENCRYPTION_SECRET to notification-agent, so saved company SMTP passwords are encrypted with the default key in shared/security/encryption.py, which is public in the repo and not refused in production. Pass a real secret before any shared deployment, then re-save the SMTP password (old ones won't decrypt).
  • Test data from these checks is still in the stack (checklist_* and recheck_* files). Run ./scripts/reset-demo.sh before the review.
  • Tests (23 Oct): 1,276 service tests pass, plus 165 + 14 root tests; frontend typecheck and mkdocs build --strict are clean.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Settings come from .env (created from .env.example on first run). The demo defaults work without editing it.

Setting Default Notes APP_ENV development (set by compose) Unset means production: default secrets refused, no demo accounts, EMAIL_MODE=dev refused JWT_SECRET, ESIGN_WEBHOOK_SECRET, RULES_ENGINE_INTERNAL_SECRET, INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD, KAFKA_PASSWORD_* published dev values Must be real secrets outside development EMAIL_MODE dev dev = Mailpit (http://localhost:8025); smtp = real delivery with SMTP_* APP_BASE_URL, PUBLIC_BASE_URL http://localhost:8080 Used for links in emails; HTTPS in production EMAIL_INTAKE_* Mailpit POP3 The mailbox documents are read from JWT_EXPIRY_MINUTES / JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRY_DAYS 15 / 7 Session lifetimes

docs.title: Business rules (no restart)
docs.text:
Thresholds and behaviour live in Business Rules (admin), not in code. Examples:

Rule Meaning approval.spend_tiers Spend tiers (auto ≤ ₹500, manager ≤ ₹5,000, then manager + finance) approval.sla_escalation_hours, approval.reminder_sla_percents Approval deadlines and reminders document.confidence_review_threshold Below this confidence a document goes to review (0.8) contract.signature_reminder_days When the signer is reminded contract.auto_send_scope Send every approved contract for signature, or only drop-folder ones document.image_preprocessing Deskew and upscale images before OCR license.anomaly_* Licence anomaly thresholds

docs.title: Company SMTP server (no restart)
docs.text: Admins set the company's own SMTP server under Email Settings (sidebar or Control Panel → Email Settings; API /api/smtp). The password is stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM) with a key derived from SMTP_ENCRYPTION_SECRET. Note: compose doesn't pass that variable to notification-agent yet, so the built-in default key is used; set it before any shared deployment.

docs.title: Notification templates (no restart)
docs.text: Control Panel → Notifications. See Control Panel.

docs.title: Drop folder
docs.text: Setting (document-vendor-agent) Default inbox_enabled true inbox_dir /inbox (the host's ./inbox) inbox_poll_seconds 3

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: The platform runs on one machine with Docker Compose (22 containers).

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Docker with Compose v2, about 8 GB of memory for Docker (ClamAV alone holds ~1 GB).
  • Internet for the first build, the breached-password check and optional model downloads.
  • Optional: Ollama on the host for the assistant (ollama pull llama3.2:3b && ollama pull nomic-embed-text).

docs.title: Start
docs.text:
./run.sh                        # builds what changed, starts everything, waits for health
./scripts/seed-demo-data.sh     # demo data
./scripts/download-models.sh    # optional: LayoutLMv3 + Legal-BERT (~1 GB)
./scripts/download-sanctions.sh # optional: sanctions list (~80 MB)
What URL App http://localhost:8080 Mailpit (all development email) http://localhost:8025 Grafana (admin / admin) http://127.0.0.1:3000 Temporal UI http://localhost:8088 MinIO console http://localhost:9001

Only port 8080 is reachable from other machines.

docs.title: After changing a service
docs.text:
docker compose up -d --build <service> <service>-worker   # workers run the service's image
docker compose up -d && docker compose restart nginx       # nginx caches upstream addresses

docs.title: Before a demo
docs.text: ./scripts/reset-demo.sh     # backs up, clears data volumes, rebuilds realistic demo data (~3 min)

docs.title: Backups
docs.text: ./scripts/backup.sh dumps Postgres and archives MinIO into .run/backups/; ./scripts/restore.sh <stamp> restores one (backing up the current data first).

docs.title: Production checklist
docs.text: Set APP_ENV=production and real secrets, put HTTPS in front of the gateway, set EMAIL_MODE=smtp, and replace placeholder role mailboxes with real distribution lists. The full list is on the dashboard's Deployment tab (docs/index.html#deploy).

docs.title: About these docs
docs.text:
This site is built with MkDocs and the Material theme from Markdown files in the repository.

What Where Pages (Markdown) docs/guide/ Site configuration: theme, navigation, search, code highlighting mkdocs.yml Diagrams and screenshots (shared with the dashboard and report) docs/assets/, docs/showcase/, published by scripts/mkdocs_hooks.py Pinned tool versions requirements-docs.txt CI build and GitHub Pages publishing .github/workflows/docs.yml

docs.title: Preview locally
docs.text:
Python 3.9–3.13 (the file watcher has no wheel for 3.15 yet):

python3.12 -m venv .venv-docs && . .venv-docs/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
mkdocs serve          # http://127.0.0.1:8000, reloads on save
mkdocs build --strict # what CI runs; fails on a broken link → .run/docs-site/

docs.title: Publish to GitHub Pages
docs.text:
Either, from a checkout with push rights:

mkdocs gh-deploy      # builds and pushes to the gh-pages branch

or on GitHub: Actions → Docs → Run workflow, tick deploy. Then, once: Settings → Pages → Source: Deploy from a branch → gh-pages / root. The site appears at https://<owner>.github.io/ProcurementAutomation/.

docs.title: Writing style
docs.text:
• Each agent page has the four parts of the standard agent template; project pages follow the overall documentation template.
  • Sentence-case headings, short paragraphs, tables for facts, one figure per idea with a numbered caption (Figure N.).
  • Names as in the app: Control Panel, Pending E-Signature, E-Signature Complete.

docs.title: How fixes are checked
docs.text:
A fix comes with a test, and the test is shown to fail when the fix is reverted. For example, the final-checklist work added:

Behaviour Test A blank scan dropped in input/ ends in failed/ with the pipeline's reason test_drop_folder.py::TestSettle An edited template is rendered in a sandbox; a broken edit falls back to the built-in test_template_store.py An SLA escalation asks the next level, not the level that missed it test_expansion_notifications.py A manager's approval of a two-level request asks finance next and generates no contract yet test_expansion_notifications.py, test_contract_documents.py::TestContractOnlyAfterFinalApproval The signer's email has a signing link test_templates.py

docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix 502 from the gateway after rebuilding a service nginx cached the old container address docker compose restart nginx A rebuild removed other containers --build re-ran the one-shot redpanda-init docker compose up -d, then check docker compose ps 429 "Too many requests" Gateway rate limit on sign-in endpoints Wait a minute 429 "Too many failed sign-in attempts" Account lockout Wait 15 minutes or reset the password Sign-up returns 503 Breached-password service unreachable Check internet access File stays in ./inbox/input Worker not running, or the file is still growing docker compose ps document-vendor-agent-worker; the file is taken once its size is stable File in ./inbox/failed Rejected or failed in the pipeline Read <file>.error.txt, or Control Panel → Documents Uploads return 503 ClamAV or MinIO down (ClamAV needs ~1 GB RAM) Raise Docker's memory; check docker compose ps First document is slow (~45 s) Models loading Wait; later ones are fast LayoutLMv3 stage "skipped: model not installed" Model not downloaded ./scripts/download-models.sh No email in Mailpit Template turned off, or consumer stopped Control Panel → Notifications (status skipped / failed); curl localhost:8004/health A Kafka event never arrived Consumer gave up after retries Control Panel → Processing and logs → Failed events Assistant doesn't answer Ollama not running on the host brew services start ollama Leftover "E2E Test Vendor" rows Test data from e2e suites ./scripts/reset-demo.sh (backs up first)
